main_text.head: CONCIO XVIII.
Deut. 23.

head.i: Non erit scortum de filiabus Israel, nec erit scortator de filiis Israel.

main_text.p: 1 Cum Deus velit sanctum habere po-pulum, prohibet non solum adulterium, sed etiam scortationem, quae contraria est sanctificationi, 1. Thessal. 4. & hominem inquinat, Marc. 7. Prohibet autem illam omni sexui, mulieribus & viris, puellis & juvenibus. Dicit enim, Non erit meretrix e filiabus Israel, neque erit scortum masculum, vel puer meritorius (ut quidam vertunt) e filiis Israel.

Errant igitur, qui in quaestionem vocant, sit ne scelus fornicatio? Si enim scelus & malum non esset, Deus non ita graviter vetuisset ac punivisset, tum hic, tum alibi, 1. Corinthiorum 6. Actor. 15. Ephes. 5. Hebr. 12. 13. Tob. 4. Sirac. 41.

2 Errant etiam qui quaerunt, quare Dominus prohibuerit simplicem fornicatione: quae quaestio & diabolica & stulta dignaq; irrisione[?] est: nam a diabolo primum talis quaestio proposita est, Gen. 3. Cur praecepit vobis Deus, inquit serpens ad mulierem, ut non come-

page.notes: The first two lines of the top paragraph and the closing word "Amen" are read from a slightly smudged scan; "Amen" may read differently. "irrisione" is read from a line-end where the printed word is partly unclear, and "est" follows a damaged word. Long s has been written as s throughout, and the "23." after "Deut." is set in a form resembling ȝ. The text of the scriptural quotation is copied as printed and was not checked against another edition.
